Spectators should be able to follow directions in their forward view without interpreting a complex map.
User requirements.Reason: Reduce map-reading effort. Supported by SR-09.

Spectators using mobility devices should be able to choose routes suited to their access needs.
User requirements.Reason: Support confidence and independent travel. Supported by SR-05.

Spectators should be able to prefer quieter or shadier routes.
User requirements.Reason: Support sensory comfort and reduced sun exposure. Supported by SR-04.

Spectators should be able to receive guidance through visual, spoken or text-based information.
User requirements.Reason: Support different communication needs. Supported by SR-09, SR-17 and SR-19.

Spectators should be able to adjust the display for their visual and motion-sensitivity needs.
User requirements.Reason: Improve readability and comfort. Supported by SR-21 and SR-22.

Spectators should be able to preview a journey at a suitable pace and viewpoint.
User requirements.Reason: Help users prepare for their visit. Supported by SR-12 and SR-14.

Spectators should be able to request appropriate human assistance.
User requirements.Reason: Provide help when navigation alone is insufficient. SR-24 currently demonstrates this only.

The system shall offer three start locations and five destinations.
System requirements.Reason: Define the supported demo journeys. Source: L605, L614.

The route calculation shall add 1.8 times segment length for modeled noise of at least 74 dB when quiet routing is selected, and 1.6 times length for unshaded segments when shade is selected.
System requirements.Reason: Make routing preferences explicit and testable. Source: L1090, L1093.

In step-free mode, the system shall exclude route segments with stairs or a modeled slope above 8.33%.
System requirements.Reason: Respect the demo’s mobility constraints. Source: L1088.

The system shall display modeled route distance, ETA, maximum slope, stair-segment count, shade coverage, average noise and elevator-use count.
System requirements.Reason: Let spectators compare route characteristics. Source: L1117, L2502.

The system shall display the selected route using first-person 3D arrows and waypoint labels.
System requirements.Reason: Support forward-view navigation. Source: L1948, L2091.

The system shall provide play/pause, route scrubbing and waypoint jumps, with preview speeds of 0.9, 1.4 and 3.2 m/s.
System requirements.Reason: Allow controlled route rehearsal. Source: L1152, L2907, L2938.

The system shall offer simulated eye heights of 1.20 m and 1.65 m.
System requirements.Reason: Preview wheelchair and standing viewpoints. Source: L2969.

The system shall offer an optional camera-video background behind the virtual route arrows.
System requirements.Reason: Demonstrate camera-overlay guidance; no real-world positioning is implemented. Source: L2566.

The system shall offer spoken route instructions and text announcements through an ARIA live region.
System requirements.Reason: Provide alternatives to visual arrows. Source: L1205, L3013.

The system shall cycle fixed English or Spanish caption text every 5.2 seconds.
System requirements.Reason: Demonstrate captions without a live event feed. Source: L2713, L2736.

The system shall offer high-contrast colors, 1.6-times arrow sizing and a 1.18-times root font scale.
System requirements.Reason: Support visual adjustment; WCAG conformance is unverified. Source: L43, L64, L1955, L3054.

The system shall offer a reduced-motion setting that suppresses decorative animation updates.
System requirements.Reason: Reduce motion-related discomfort; route playback can continue. Source: L3086, L3229.

The system shall show an assistance-type selector and a preset confirmation in a local request dialog.
System requirements.Reason: Demonstrate an assistance workflow; no request is sent. Source: L789, L3111, L3123.
